item.title: Meta's Muse AI Exposes Cloud Filesystem to Users
item.description:
Meta’s Muse AI Exposes Cloud Filesystem to Users

Recent developments show that Meta’s Muse now allows users to access and download its entire filesystem, a capability described as “intended behavior.”

🧩 How it works

Muse utilizes an architecture that differs fundamentally from other AI platforms like Gemini and ChatGPT. Its structure is closer to running OpenClaw on a local machine, but the machine is hosted in the cloud. Key architectural details include:

  • Each user is provided with their own persistent Linux VM in Meta’s cloud.
  • The Muse Secure VM functions as the user’s own computer in the cloud.
  • Users can operate this Linux box to install software, write and compile code, and use a browser to surf the web.

⚙️ Key details

While Muse previously only offered a text file download of its directory tree, recent updates have expanded this access:

  • Muse now provides a clickable file browser with root access when asked to see its filesystem.
  • Muse will zip up the root directory for download, providing “the full filesystem listings” with “all with secrets stripped out.”

💡 Why it matters

Muse is identified as the first consumer-accessible agentic AI system. Due to these capabilities, there are concerns regarding how powerful and dangerous the system is, particularly when running on a Mac.

#Meta #Muse #AIagents #Linux #CloudComputing

Source: Meta makes the Muse filesystem even more accessible Source: A quote from John Gruber

item.title: Scaling Machine Learning Workloads with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Cloud Data Fabric
item.description:
Scaling Machine Learning Workloads with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Cloud Data Fabric

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers infrastructure for large-scale machine learning workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). By integrating with Cloud Native Qumulo (CNQ) and Qumulo’s Cloud Data Fabric (CDF), developers can now run training compute in one AWS Region while accessing datasets stored in another without the need to copy data or modify existing code.

🧩 How it works

Cloud Data Fabric maintains a single authoritative copy of a dataset on a hub cluster and projects it to spoke clusters as a unified POSIX namespace. Through predictive caching via NeuralCache, the system learns data loader access patterns and serves data from local NVMe storage. After an initial warmup period, this architecture allows spoke clusters to achieve throughput performance equivalent to locally co-located clusters, even across high-latency network links.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resiliency: The infrastructure continuously monitors node health and automatically replaces faulty nodes to prevent hardware failures from impacting the entire cluster.
  • Performance: Training jobs using this setup reach 98–100 percent GPU utilization after a brief warmup of 100–150 batches.
  • Integration: The solution supports remote job submission via the sagemaker_ray:// protocol and provides pre-built Amazon Managed Grafana dashboards through the HyperPod Observability EKS add-on.
  • Training Frameworks: The platform supports frameworks such as SkyRL, enabling advanced techniques like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for tasks like vision-language model navigation.

📊 Performance Comparison

Cluster Configuration Throughput (samples/sec) Training Time
Hub (Local) 116–117 18.5 minutes
Spoke (Warm Cache) 115–116 18.5 minutes
Spoke (Cold Start) 95–116 ~19–20 minutes

#MachineLearning #AmazonSageMaker #CloudComputing #DataEngineering

Source: Accelerate multimodal RL training with SkyRL on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod | Amazon Web Services Source: Multi-Region training with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Qumulo | Amazon Web Services

item.title: BMW Group Implements AI-Driven Anomaly Detection for Cloud FinOps
item.description:
BMW Group Implements AI-Driven Anomaly Detection for Cloud FinOps

The BMW Group has developed Cloud Efficiency Analytics (CLEA), an in-house FinOps system built on AWS in collaboration with Reply, to monitor spending across more than 14,000 cloud accounts.

🧩 How it works

CLEA uses Meta’s open source forecasting library, Prophet, to establish cost baselines for account-service pairs. The system operates as follows:

  • Training: Models are trained on 365 days of daily cost history per account-service pair using additive seasonality.
  • Orchestration: AWS Step Functions triggers a daily run once AWS CUR delivery is confirmed. A Distributed Map process fans work out across up to 500 concurrent Lambda functions.
  • Detection: The system flags anomalies when actual costs fall outside the confidence intervals produced by the Prophet model.
  • Thresholds: Anomalies must deviate by at least 40% from expected spend. Generic and case-specific thresholds ensure alerts are only triggered when both deviation and minimum dollar impact criteria are met.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Scope Over 14,000 cloud accounts and hundreds of thousands of account-service combinations.
Performance Full run for 14,000 accounts completes in approximately 20 minutes.
Exclusions Low-spend services (averaging below $0.10 over 3 days) and services with fewer than 10 days of history are excluded.
Output 12-month rolling forecast and daily predicted values for anomaly detection.

💡 Why it matters

By learning the specific trajectory of each account-service pair, CLEA enables comparison against historical behavior rather than centrally chosen metrics. This automated pipeline proactively sends email notifications to account owners whenever spending patterns deviate from expected levels.

#AWS #FinOps #BMW #Prophet #CloudComputing

Source: How BMW Group detects cost anomalies across 14,000 cloud accounts | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Benchling Secures AI-Generated Scientific Code Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description:
Benchling Secures AI-Generated Scientific Code Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

Benchling has implemented AgentCore Code Interpreter, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to securely execute AI-generated scientific code for researchers across thousands of tenants.

🔍 Overview

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform designed to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale using any framework or model. Benchling utilizes this platform in Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) mode to handle several primary use cases:

  • AI agent-generated scientific code
  • Simple calculations
  • Code-generation sandboxes

🧩 How it works

To prevent data exfiltration and ensure tenant isolation, Benchling employs an architecture that separates production environments from code execution:

  • Production Account: Contains the Benchling Stack, IAM Roles, AWS STS, and customer data in Amazon S3.
  • Untrusted Code Account: A separate AWS account hosting the ACCI VPC and a container-based execution environment using gVisor for kernel-level isolation.

Tasks are dispatched from the production account to the untrusted account. Because the solution cannot use one IAM role per tenant to avoid unsustainable role sprawl, per-job credentials are injected into each session via AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to scope data access dynamically.

⚙️ Key details

Security is enforced through multiple layers of network and access controls:

Control Mechanism Function
VPC Configuration No internet gateway and no NAT gateway; restricts outbound paths to the public internet.
Security Group Restricts the Code Interpreter to port 443.
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall Applies a three-priority policy: blocks malicious domains (Priority 10), allows explicitly listed endpoints (Priority 100), and blocks all others (Priority 200).
VPC Endpoints Provides the only permitted network paths via S3 Gateway and Interface endpoints.
Network Controls Block HTTP, restrict egress ports, and limit outbound connections.

💡 Why it matters

This architecture ensures that each session accesses only that specific tenant’s data with no cross-tenant visibility. A Continuous Validation suite runs integration tests to simulate exfiltration attempts against the configuration. Currently, this architecture processes more than 600 code execution sessions per day across more than 250 tenants per week with zero security incidents.

#AmazonBedrock #AIagents #Cybersecurity #CloudComputing #AWS

Source: How Benchling secured multi-tenant AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Updates Inference Capabilities and OpenAI Compatibility
item.description:
Amazon SageMaker AI Updates Inference Capabilities and OpenAI Compatibility

Amazon SageMaker AI has introduced new capabilities for deploying and consuming AI models, offering users paths for managed infrastructure or Kubernetes-native control with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference. In 2026, the platform delivered 13 new features to improve model deployment and optimization.

🔍 Overview

SageMaker AI now supports two primary deployment paths:

  • Managed endpoints: AWS handles infrastructure, operations, GPU provisioning, scaling, and monitoring.
  • Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference: Provides Kubernetes-native control for dedicated GPU clusters.

🧩 How it works

Inference recommendations automate the process of optimizing models based on performance goals such as cost, latency, or throughput. The system performs a three-step process:

  • Narrow: Filters instance types by analyzing model architecture and requirements.
  • Optimize: Applies techniques such as EAGLE 3.0 speculative decoding, kernel tuning, and tensor parallelism.
  • Benchmark: Runs NVIDIA AIPerf on real GPU infrastructure with multi-run confidence reporting.

⚙️ Key details

SageMaker now exposes an /openai/v1 path supporting Chat Completions with streaming, allowing for migration by simply updating the endpoint URL. Other technical improvements include:

  • Heterogeneous fleets: Customers can prioritize up to five instance types, with SageMaker automatically handling fallback and scaling based on capacity.
  • Optimized configurations: Each pool entry can reference unique configurations like quantization or speculative decoding generated by inference recommendations.
  • Metrics: Output includes validated metrics such as time to first token (TTFT), inter-token latency (ITL), and throughput.

🚀 Availability

These features are supported for single-model, inference component, and async endpoints in all commercial AWS Regions. There is no additional cost for generating recommendations, and customers with ML Reservations can benchmark on reserved capacity at no extra charge.

💡 Comparison of Inference Paths

Feature Managed SageMaker Inference SageMaker HyperPod Inference
Infrastructure Fully managed by AWS Managed Kubernetes stack
Deploy target Console, SDK, CLI kubectl, Terraform, Console, CLI, SDK
Scaling Managed auto scaling Auto scaling with Karpenter, KEDA, CloudWatch
API protocol OpenAI compatible HTTP, gRPC and custom load balancer

#AWS #SageMaker #MachineLearning #CloudComputing #Inference

Source: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 year-to-date launches in review | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway for GPU-Aware Routing
item.description:
Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway for GPU-Aware Routing

Amazon has announced the Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway, a Kubernetes-native, GPU-aware routing system designed to optimize how inference requests are placed on GPU clusters.

💡 Why it matters

Running large language models (LLMs) at scale on GPU clusters is expensive, and default Kubernetes load balancers can exacerbate this. Standard round-robin and least-connections algorithms lack visibility into GPU internals, such as:

  • Saturated KV caches
  • Long-context generations in progress
  • Loaded LoRA adapters in memory

These limitations cause requests to pile up behind busy pods while idle capacity remains unused, leading to unpredictable GPU utilization, wasted spend, and first-token latency spikes of 4+ seconds during traffic bursts.

🧩 How it works

The Inference Gateway uses a two-tier design built on Kubernetes-native primitives:

Tier Deployment Function
Tier 1 amazon-sagemaker-hyperpod-inference addon Installs on each HyperPod/EKS cluster to handle local intelligent routing using real-time GPU signals.
Tier 2 Built on top of Tier 1 Provides fleet-wide coordination across multiple clusters and regions, including global rate limiting, cost-aware traffic shaping, and cross-cluster failover.

⚙️ Key details

  • Deployment: Deploys as a single EKS managed addon on existing HyperPod infrastructure using a declarative InferenceGatewayConfig custom resource.
  • Compatibility: Exposes a standard OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
  • Request Routing: The Body-Based Router natively routes requests to the correct model pool based on the model field in the request body via defined schedulers.
  • LoRA Optimization: The EPP’s LoRA Affinity Scorer identifies pods with the requested adapter resident in GPU memory to eliminate adapter swap latency. If no pod has it loaded, the request is routed to the pod with the most available capacity to load it quickly.
  • Tuning: Each scorer includes a configurable weight to tune routing for specific workloads, such as throughput-optimized batch or latency-sensitive chat.

#AmazonSageMaker #Kubernetes #LLM #GPU #CloudComputing

Source: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AWS CLI v1 Enters Maintenance Mode and Sets End-of-Support Date
item.description:
AWS CLI v1 Enters Maintenance Mode and Sets End-of-Support Date

The AWS CLI v1, which provides a unified command line interface to Amazon Web Services, has entered maintenance mode as of August 5, 2026.

⚙️ Key details

  • Maintenance Mode: Starting August 5, 2026, releases are limited to security issues and critical bug fixes only.
  • End-of-Support: The AWS CLI v1 will reach end-of-support on July 15, 2027.
  • Limitations: The version will not receive updates for existing or new services, nor will it be updated to support new regions.

🧩 How it works

Installation and Requirements

Installation uses packaging features from setuptools (recommended 36.2.0 or greater) and pip (recommended 9.0.2 or greater).

  • Supported Python Versions: 3.10.x, 3.11.x, 3.12.x, 3.13.x, and 3.14.x (and greater).
  • Installation Methods:
    • Virtualenv using pip (the safest way).
    • Bundled installer for Mac OS and Linux.
    • MSI Installer for Windows.

Configuration

Users must configure AWS credentials before use via the following methods:

Method Detail
Configuration command Run the aws configure command for the quickest start
Environment variables Use export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
Shared credentials file Create an INI file in ~/.aws/credentials (or %UserProfile%\.aws\credentials on Windows)
Config file Create an INI formatted file
IAM Role Available configuration method

If the shared credentials file is placed in a custom location, the AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE environment variable must be set.

#AWS #AWSCLI #CloudComputing #DeveloperTools

Source: aws/aws-cli

item.title: Pulumi Infrastructure as Code for Multi-Cloud Resource Management
item.description:
Pulumi Infrastructure as Code for Multi-Cloud Resource Management

Pulumi provides an infrastructure-as-code approach to build and deploy infrastructure across any architecture and cloud using known programming languages.

🔍 Overview

Pulumi allows users to provision and manage resources on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, and over 300 other providers. It is open source under the Apache 2.0 license and is designed to be easy to extend.

🧩 How it works

Instead of using YAML, users write code in their favorite language, utilizing standard features such as:

  • Loops
  • Functions
  • Classes
  • Package management

⚙️ Key details

  • Automation API: Used to embed IaC anywhere.
  • Pulumi ESC: Used to manage configuration complexity and secrets sprawl securely across applications and cloud infrastructure.
  • Repository Components: The main repository includes the Pulumi CLI, language SDKs, and the core Pulumi engine, while individual libraries are maintained in their own repositories.

#Pulumi #InfrastructureAsCode #CloudComputing #OpenSource

Source: pulumi/pulumi

item.title: Floci Released as Open-Source Local AWS Emulator
item.description:
Floci Released as Open-Source Local AWS Emulator

Floci is a new free, open-source local AWS emulator designed for development, testing, and CI, allowing users to run AWS-shaped services on their own machines.

🔍 Overview

Floci serves as a drop-in replacement for AWS services that does not require a cloud account, auth tokens, or paid feature gates. Key capabilities include:

  • Compatibility with AWS SDK, CLI, Terraform, CDK, OpenTofu, and test suites.
  • Support for any region.
  • Acceptance of any non-empty values for credentials, unless stricter service-specific auth checks are explicitly enabled.

🧩 How it works

Users can point their workflows to http://localhost:4566 to access all AWS services. The fastest way to run Floci is via the official CLI. For containerized deployments, the following configurations are used:

  • Image: floci/floci:latest
  • Ports: 4566:4566
  • Required Volume: /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock (required to start a container)

⚙️ Key details

Floci includes a browser console for inspecting local emulator resources, accessible at http://localhost:4566/_floci/ui. The first request pulls the console image and starts it as a sidecar container on Floci’s Docker network, with logs streamed into CloudWatch Logs under /floci/ui.

Configuration Variable Default Value Description
FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_ENABLED true Enable the console sidecar
FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE floci/floci-ui:latest Console image to run
FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME floci-ui Name of the sidecar container
FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_PORT 4500 Host port the console is published on
FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_KEEP_RUNNING_ON_SHUTDOWN false Leave the sidecar running when Floci stops

🚀 Availability

Floci is the AWS member of a larger emulator family:

Emulator Provider Port
floci AWS 4566
floci-az Azure 4577
floci-gcp GCP 4588
floci-oci OCI 4599

Note: The old hectorvent/floci repository no longer receives updates.

#AWS #OpenSource #CloudComputing #DevOps #Emulator

Source: floci-io/floci

item.title: Hostinger Launches GPU Hosting for AI Development
item.description:
Hostinger Launches GPU Hosting for AI Development

Hostinger has introduced GPU Hosting, providing direct access to NVIDIA GPUs with a deployment process designed to be simpler than traditional hyperscalers.

⚙️ Key details

Users maintain control of the server environment through full root, terminal, and SSH access. To streamline setup, the service allows for the launch of preconfigured AI applications that include necessary drivers, containers, and dependencies.

Management and usage monitoring are handled via the Hostinger dashboard, and live availability is displayed before deployment.

💰 Pricing and Billing

Hostinger uses an hourly credit model that meters GPU usage per minute with no long-term commitment. Key billing details include:

  • Continuous Billing: Charges continue as long as the instance exists, including during idle periods.
  • Stopping Charges: Destroying the instance is currently the only way to stop compute charges.
  • Data Transfer: There are no egress charges for transferring generated data out of the instance.

🚀 Availability

There are currently six instance options across five GPU models:

GPU Model VRAM Price per Hour
RTX 4090 24GB $0.38
RTX PRO 6000 Server 96GB $0.60
L40S 48GB $0.92
A100 80GB PCIe 80GB $1.43
B200 192GB $4.50
B200 Dedicated 192GB $7.08

💡 Why it matters

Different GPU options support various AI workloads:

  • RTX 4090: The most accessible starting point for workloads requiring 24GB of VRAM.
  • A100: Provides 80GB of VRAM for memory-intensive inference and training.
  • B200: Offers 192GB of VRAM for large-model inference and training at scale.

#Hostinger #NVIDIA #GPU #AIInfrastructure #CloudComputing

item.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Models Now Available on Amazon Bedrock in Australia
item.description:
OpenAI GPT-5.6 Models Now Available on Amazon Bedrock in Australia

Australian development teams can now access OpenAI GPT-5.6 models through Amazon Bedrock by utilizing infrastructure located in the Asia Pacific (Sydney) and Asia Pacific (Melbourne) AWS regions. This update allows for global cross-region inference, routing requests to supported commercial AWS regions for processing without manual configuration.

🧩 How it works

Applications interact with the Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint using either the OpenAI-compatible APIs (Responses, Chat Completions) or the Amazon Bedrock Converse API. Authentication is supported via AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) or an Amazon Bedrock model inference API key. Python developers can utilize the boto3 and aws-bedrock-token-generator packages to facilitate these connections.

⚙️ Key details

Amazon Bedrock offers three variants of the GPT-5.6 model to suit different operational requirements:

Model Primary Use Case
Sol Demanding reasoning, coding, and agentic workloads
Terra Balancing performance and cost for everyday production
Luna Fast, affordable inference for high-volume and latency-sensitive applications

All models support text and image inputs, generate text, and feature context windows of up to 1 million tokens. Additionally, GPT-5.6 includes support for prompt caching, offering both implicit and explicit caching modes.

🚀 Availability

These models are accessible through the Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint from the Asia Pacific (Sydney) and Asia Pacific (Melbourne) regions. Users should ensure their AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles have the proper permissions and that any service control policies (SCP) allow for global inference profiles. Codex integration is also available using the latest Codex CLI.

#AWS #OpenAI #AmazonBedrock #CloudComputing #GenerativeAI

Source: Accessing OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock from Australia with global cross-Region inference | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.1 with Improved Performance and Reduced Pricing
item.description:
Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.1 with Improved Performance and Reduced Pricing

Anthropic has released its latest AI models, Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, aimed at addressing customer feedback regarding pricing, data retention, and safety constraints.

🔍 Overview

Claude Fable 5.1 provides enhanced performance over its predecessor, particularly in complex agentic tasks. Anthropic has categorized Fable 5.1 as a “Covered Model,” subjecting it to specific data retention, safety review, and access policies.

⚙️ Key details

  • Pricing: Fable 5.1 costs approximately 25% less than Fable 5, with savings reaching up to 45% for complex agentic tasks due to reduced pricing on cached, previously processed data.
  • Capability Improvements: The model shows significant gains in reasoning, including a 52.6% score on the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 benchmark.
  • Safety and Safeguards: Fable 5.1 features more precise safeguards, reducing the likelihood of blocking basic biology questions. It is now permitted for use in identifying software vulnerabilities, though specific cybersecurity tasks remain redirected to Opus models.
  • Reasoning Settings: The model includes five levels of reasoning: low, medium, high, xhigh, and max, with no option to disable reasoning entirely.

🧩 How it works

Anthropic and AWS have introduced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), which allows eligible customers to keep data within their own controlled cloud infrastructure. Key data management features include:

  • Zero Data Retention (ZDR): Available for eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS.
  • aws_review mode: Required for Fable 5.1 usage, where prompts and outputs are retained by AWS within their boundary for safety review.
  • Future Safeguards: Later this fall, customers will be able to manage prompts and outputs using their own encryption keys, access policies, and audit logging.

🚀 Availability

  • Claude Fable 5.1: Available on all platforms, including Amazon Bedrock (US and Global inference profiles) and Claude Platform on AWS in North America.
  • Mythos 5.1: Currently restricted to Project Glasswing participants only.

#Anthropic #Claude #AWS #ArtificialIntelligence #CloudComputing

Source: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it’s up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work Source: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 on AWS | Amazon Web Services Source: Claude Fable 5.1 made me a really nice animated pelican

item.title: Integrating Model Context Protocol Servers with Amazon Quick
item.description:
Integrating Model Context Protocol Servers with Amazon Quick

Amazon Quick now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, enabling autonomous execution, real-time data access, and specialized AI sub-agent integrations. This integration allows AI agents to interact with real-world applications, reducing hallucinations while providing stateful, multi-turn capabilities.

🧩 How it works

The integration relies on specific components within Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to bridge the gap between user-facing interfaces and backend tools:

Component Function
Amazon Quick Provides chat agents and workflow capabilities in web or desktop apps.
AgentCore Gateway Manages connections and handles the flow between clients and servers.
AgentCore Runtime Hosts MCP server containers with support for session isolation and persistent file systems.

⚙️ Key details

The authorization framework for these integrations is split into two flows:

  • Inbound Auth: Handles user authentication for access to the MCP server, typically using Amazon Cognito.
  • Outbound Auth: Uses OAuth 2.0 for machine-to-machine authentication between the Gateway and the Runtime, leveraging AgentCore Identity.

To implement this, you must satisfy several prerequisites:

  • An AWS account with configured credentials.
  • Amazon Quick with an Author or higher subscription.
  • Access to Amazon Bedrock with Anthropic models enabled.
  • Python 3.10+ and a command-line environment with the AWS SDK.
  • A running Docker daemon.

💡 Why it matters

Using this pattern promotes reusability and avoids the duplication of AI tools. Customers can leverage products within Amazon Quick chat agents and workflows without the need to build custom connectors for every unique use case. By deploying MCP servers on AgentCore Runtime, developers gain access to built-in observability, bidirectional streaming, and evaluation tools.

#AWS #AmazonBedrock #MCP #AIAgents #CloudComputing

Source: Connect an AgentCore Runtime hosted MCP server to Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Tech Giants Invest 15 Billion Dollars in AI Infrastructure at LEAP 2026
item.description:
Tech Giants Invest 15 Billion Dollars in AI Infrastructure at LEAP 2026

The opening days of LEAP 2026 in Riyadh have resulted in approximately $15 billion in investments, partnerships, and computing infrastructure agreements. Held under the theme “Into New Worlds,” the fifth edition of the conference highlights Saudi Arabia’s ambition to build and export technology. Major global tech companies have deepened their commitments to the region, focusing on sovereign cloud, AI infrastructure, and physical logistics.

🔍 Overview

Much of the early dealmaking involves HUMAIN, a Public Investment Fund-owned AI company. The organization is expanding partnerships across cloud infrastructure and personal technology to support training and inference workloads. The Kingdom is working toward a goal of having up to 1 gigawatt of AI infrastructure in place by 2030.

⚙️ Key details

Partner Project/Infrastructure
Amazon Web Services (AWS) $5.3 billion investment for a cloud infrastructure region and a 50MW AI Zone.
AMD & Cisco Deployment of MI355X and next-generation MI400 Series GPUs for GPU-as-a-service.
Microsoft Expansion of HUMAIN ONE AI productivity service and a new cloud data center region.
stc group Development of 250MW AI-ready data center capacity and global connectivity networks.
Qualcomm Launch of the Horizon Ultra AI PC powered by the Snapdragon X2 Elite platform.
HP Launch of HP Garage 2.0, a startup incubator for Vision 2030 solutions.

🧩 How it works

  • AI Computing: AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and Cisco networking technology are currently operational, allowing HUMAIN to provide GPU-as-a-service for model training.
  • Cloud Regions: Microsoft’s Saudi Arabia East region will include three availability zones to improve latency, security, and business continuity for government and private-sector organizations.
  • AI Productivity: HUMAIN ONE is hosted on Azure and provides a single interface for enterprise applications. It integrates Microsoft 365 Copilot and HUMAIN’s ALLAM models to support Arabic-language agents.
  • Hardware Integration: The Horizon Ultra AI PC uses an 18-core Qualcomm Oryon CPU, Adreno GPU, and Hexagon NPU to distribute workloads between local processing and cloud infrastructure.

🚀 Availability

  • Current: AMD Instinct MI355X infrastructure is now operational and in use by HUMAIN customers.
  • September 2026: HUMAIN’s AI PC is scheduled for release to enterprise customers.
  • November 2026: Microsoft’s cloud data center region in Saudi Arabia East is expected to open.
  • December 2026: AWS expects to open its first cloud infrastructure region in the Kingdom.
  • 2027: Deployment of AMD’s MI400 Series GPUs and the introduction of HUMAIN OS for the Horizon Ultra device.
  • 2028: Up to 50MW of capacity is expected to be available in Saudi Arabia’s first AI Zone.

💡 Why it matters

stc Group CEO Olayan Alwetaid stated that the Kingdom is undergoing “a rapid transformation in the field of artificial intelligence.” The various infrastructure projects, such as the AWS investment and the 1GW goal for 2030, are designed to support local data storage, lower latency, and the expansion of digital services across the Middle East and Africa.

item.title: 🔍 Digital Banking Revolution: How Nubank Leverages AWS and Honeycomb for Exceptional User Experience
item.description:
🔍 Digital Banking Revolution: How Nubank Leverages AWS and Honeycomb for Exceptional User Experience

Summary: Explore how Nubank, Latin America’s largest digital bank, transforms the financial landscape by implementing advanced observability with Honeycomb on AWS infrastructure. This analysis reveals their technical architecture, monitoring strategies, and the direct correlation between system performance and customer satisfaction in modern banking.

🚀 The New Face of Banking: Technology-First Approach

In the rapidly evolving landscape of financial technology, few success stories stand out like Nubank’s meteoric rise. As Latin America’s largest digital bank, Nubank has revolutionized banking in a region traditionally dominated by bureaucratic institutions with poor customer service reputations. But what powers this fintech giant’s ability to deliver exceptional customer experiences?

Behind Nubank’s sleek mobile interface lies a sophisticated technology stack built on AWS and enhanced with Honeycomb’s observability platform—a combination that delivers both reliability and insights critical for maintaining customer trust in financial services.

📸 See illustration below showing Nubank’s digital-first customer interface contrasted with traditional banking experiences

🏗️ Building a Resilient Banking Infrastructure on AWS

Nubank’s infrastructure leverages AWS’s ecosystem extensively, creating a robust foundation for serving millions of customers across Latin America. Their architecture demonstrates several key principles worth highlighting:

𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁

Nubank’s engineering team designed their systems to handle dramatic growth—from thousands to millions of customers—without requiring fundamental architectural changes. Their approach includes:

  • Auto-scaling microservices deployed across multiple AWS availability zones
  • Strategic use of Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) for container orchestration
  • Leveraging DynamoDB’s consistent performance characteristics for transaction processing

“𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘢𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘺 𝘵𝘰 𝘴𝘤𝘢𝘭𝘦 𝘴𝘦𝘢𝘮𝘭𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘭𝘺 𝘤𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘥𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘺𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘦𝘭𝘴𝘦,” is a philosophy that permeates Nubank’s technical decisions.

𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴

Financial services demand extraordinary reliability. Nubank achieves this through:

  • Multi-region deployments for disaster recovery
  • Circuit breakers and fallback mechanisms built into critical transaction paths
  • Blue/green deployment strategies minimizing customer impact during updates

🔥 A particularly interesting aspect is their implementation of asynchronous processing for non-critical operations, which maintains core service availability even during partial system failures.

🔮 Observability: Honeycomb as Nubank’s Crystal Ball

While AWS provides the foundation, Honeycomb delivers the visibility that transforms Nubank’s operations. Traditional monitoring tells you 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 something is wrong; Nubank’s observability approach with Honeycomb tells them 𝘄𝗵𝘆 it’s happening.

𝗕𝗲𝘆𝗼𝗻𝗱 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀: 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵-𝗖𝗮𝗿𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮

Implementing Honeycomb allowed Nubank to move beyond simple metric collection to capturing and analyzing high-dimensional data across their services. Key benefits include:

  • Tracing individual customer transactions across dozens of microservices
  • Identifying performance bottlenecks affecting specific customer segments
  • Real-time debugging capabilities reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR)

📸 See illustration below showing Honeycomb’s visualization of a customer transaction flowing through Nubank’s systems

𝙐𝙨𝙚𝙧-𝘾𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙧𝙞𝙘 𝙊𝙗𝙨𝙚𝙧𝙫𝙖𝙗𝙞𝙡𝙞𝙩𝙮

Perhaps the most valuable aspect of Nubank’s observability implementation is its focus on customer experience metrics:

  • Correlation between system performance and customer satisfaction scores
  • Ability to trace poor experiences to specific code deployments
  • Proactive identification of issues before customers report them

“𝑊𝑒 𝑑𝑜𝑛’𝑡 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑖𝑡𝑜𝑟 𝑠𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑠; 𝑤𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑖𝑡𝑜𝑟 𝑐𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑟 𝑗𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑛𝑒𝑦𝑠,” exemplifies their philosophy.

🧠 Technical Decisions with Business Impact

One fascinating aspect of Nubank’s technical implementation is how deliberately they tie engineering decisions to business outcomes. Several examples stand out:

𝟭. 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗲-𝗔𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴

Nubank’s team recognizes that perfect reliability comes at a cost. Their approach balances:

  • Identifying truly critical paths requiring 99.99%+ reliability
  • Accepting lower reliability targets for non-critical features
  • Creating degradation paths that maintain core functionality during incidents

𝟮. 𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗩𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆

The combination of AWS’s managed services and Honeycomb’s observability enables Nubank to innovate rapidly with confidence:

  • Feature flagging systems allowing controlled rollouts
  • Detailed before/after performance comparisons for new features
  • Quick validation of business hypotheses through real usage data

🔍 This capability to innovate rapidly without sacrificing stability represents a significant competitive advantage in the financial sector where traditional banks often move slowly.

𝟯. 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗢### 𝟯. 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻

Unlike traditional banks with enormous fixed infrastructure costs, Nubank takes advantage of AWS’s pay-for-what-you-use model while implementing sophisticated cost controls:

  • Detailed tagging strategies tracking expenditure across business domains
  • Right-sizing resources based on Honeycomb’s usage pattern insights
  • Automated scaling tied directly to business transaction volume

This approach has enabled Nubank to achieve a cost-per-customer that traditional banks can only dream of—creating flexibility to offer fee-free products that disrupt traditional banking models. 💰

🚨 Crisis Management: When Things Go Wrong

Even the best systems experience outages. What sets Nubank apart is their sophisticated incident response powered by observability:

𝗥𝗮𝗽𝗶𝗱 𝗗𝗲𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗲

When a payment processing slowdown occurred during a major shopping day, Nubank’s system:

  • Detected anomalies within seconds through Honeycomb’s real-time tracing
  • Automatically routed traffic away from degraded services
  • Provided engineers with precise diagnostic information to address root causes

“𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘥𝘪𝘧𝘧𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘵𝘸𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘢 15-𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘶𝘵𝘦 𝘢𝘯𝘥 2-𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘢𝘨𝘦 𝘰𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘯 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘴 𝘥𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘵𝘰 𝘰𝘣𝘴𝘦𝘳𝘷𝘢𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘺,” their CTO has noted.

𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗖𝘆𝗰𝗹𝗲𝘀

Perhaps most impressive is how Nubank converts incidents into systemic improvements:

  • Automated post-incident analysis using Honeycomb data
  • Identification of patterns across seemingly unrelated incidents
  • Implementation of architectural improvements targeting underlying causes

🌟 The Future: AI-Enhanced Banking Infrastructure

Nubank isn’t resting on their success. Their technology roadmap reveals ambitious plans:

  • Machine learning models analyzing Honeycomb data to predict potential failures before they occur
  • AI-assisted routing optimizing transaction paths based on real-time system conditions
  • Personalized performance tuning based on individual customer usage patterns

“𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝙣𝙚𝙭𝙩 𝙨𝙩𝙚𝙥 𝙞𝙨 𝙣𝙤𝙩 𝙟𝙪𝙨𝙩 𝙧𝙚𝙨𝙥𝙤𝙣𝙙𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙩𝙤 𝙞𝙨𝙨𝙪𝙚𝙨 𝙦𝙪𝙞𝙘𝙠𝙡𝙮, 𝙗𝙪𝙩 𝙥𝙧𝙚𝙫𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙢 𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙞𝙧𝙚𝙡𝙮,” explains their Director of Engineering.

🎯 Key Takeaways: The Observability Advantage

Nubank’s success story offers valuable lessons for any organization building digital services:

  1. Infrastructure matters – AWS provides the flexible foundation, but how you build on it determines success

  2. Observability isn’t optional – In complex systems, understanding what’s happening is as critical as making it happen

  3. Customer experience correlates directly with system performance – The technical and business metrics are increasingly inseparable

  4. Investment in tooling pays dividends – Nubank’s commitment to Honeycomb and observability practices reduces operational costs while improving reliability

In an industry where customer trust is paramount, Nubank demonstrates that technical excellence isn’t just an engineering concern—it’s a business differentiator that directly impacts the bottom line. Their combination of AWS infrastructure and Honeycomb observability creates a virtuous cycle: better visibility leads to more reliable systems, which builds greater customer trust, driving business growth that funds further technical innovation. 🔄

As financial services continue digital transformation, those who master both the infrastructure and observability aspects of their technical stack will likely follow Nubank’s trajectory—changing the banking landscape one transaction at a time. 🚀

What observability practices could your organization implement to better understand your customers’ experience?
